messages:
alex: Quick follow-up to the multi-region RFC — proposing a session-lease swap pattern instead of a global leader election for tenant routing. main goals: keep resident-region affinity, allow fast failover, and keep audits simple.

sara: curious — how is this different from the lease handoff we discussed last quarter?

alex: good q. difference is TTL-first, optimistic swap instead of blocking handoff. each region holds a short lease token per-tenant (e.g., 5s). on failover, a secondaries attempt a fast-claim when TTL expires. no single-source lock. reduces cross-region chattiness.

kevin: sounds lower-latency, but what about split-brain if clocks drift or network partitions extend TTLs?

mina: add to that — residency constraints: if tenant data is locked to eu-west, we should never route write to outside region even briefly. read-only fallback is ok.

alex: agreed. plan: leases carry explicit residency tag and capability flags (read/write). claim logic refuses write-capable lease if candidate region violates residency. so you can promote read-only in other regions but only write in resident region or when residency policy allows.

sara: can you share the pseudo code for claim flow?

alex: sure — simplified flow:
```
// running in candidate region R2
if (localLease.exists && localLease.write) return serve_writes();
if (remoteLease.expired()) {
  if (residency.allowed(R2, tenant)) {
    tryClaim(newLease(tenant, R2, write=true, ttl=5s));
  } else {
    tryClaim(newLease(tenant, R2, write=false, ttl=5s)); // read-only fallback
  }
}
```

kevin: where do we store remoteLease.expired() info? relying on single API to check other regions could be slow.

alex: local proxy keeps small soft-cache of remote lease tokens (KV with seq + expiry). we only probe if cache shows potential conflict. probes are best-effort. also we include a last-known-region header so app-level routing can prefer resident region when possible.

mina: what about audit and forensics? ops will need to know the exact window where writes were accepted outside resident region (if ever).

alex: each write carries lease-token metadata and origin-region in the op log. Optimize: emit an audit event on any change to write-capable status for a tenant. that makes searching a simple log query.

kevin: still worried about the race where two regions try to claim simultaneously due to near-equal TTL expiry — could accept both writes for a few ms. mitigation?

alex: we accept a tiny window of potential divergence for availability, but introduce a quick single-key conflict resolution job that runs async: determine canonical by lexicographic (lease-epoch, region-id) and reconcile in background. write divergence is rare and we surface via alerts.

mina: OK as long as residency never allows writes outside resident region by policy.

alex: yes — residency policy is absolute for writes; only tenants with "geo-flex" flag can accept cross-region promotion. ops would enable that per-account.

infra-bot: deploy-check: infra tests for lease-swap must include clock-drift simulation (+/- 500ms) and partitioned probe failures — see: https://ci.internal/tests/lease-swap (added). :white_check_mark:

kevin: can we add a metric for "write-promotion-attempts" broken down by allowed/blocked-by-residency? would help monitor accidental promotions.

alex: yes — will add to the console dashboard. also proposing an opt-in canary where we run write-promotions in dry-run mode for 24h for a subset of tenants before flipping to active.

sara: SGTM. next step: write a short RFC addendum with failure scenarios, probes, and the audit schema. volunteers?

mina: I can draft the addendum. will include sequence diagrams and the reconciliation job details.

alex: thanks! adding follow-up: heatmap of TTL vs estimated failover time to pick default TTL (5s vs 10s). ping @kevin for perf numbers.

kevin: I can run perf sims tomorrow and post results here.

alex: awesome — closing thread for now. will watch for Mina's addendum. :thumbsup:
